wages.text: Garamendi pushed to force a House vote on raising the federal minimum wage.
wages.quote: Increasing the minimum wage is one of the most effective methods we have to lift millions of Americans out of poverty

trade.text: Garamendi helped secure retaliatory tariffs on certain European canned fruit imports and supported measures to protect domestic industry.
trade.quote: Also, helped secure new retaliatory tariffs on canned peaches and mixed fruits from the European Union.

debt.text: Garamendi flatly opposed cutting Social Security, Medicare or Medicaid as part of debt-ceiling talks.
debt.quote: We have no right at this time, or any time in the future, to harm those who are on Social Security.

housing.text: Garamendi makes lowering housing prices and expanding affordable housing supply a top priority and advocates more funding for housing programs.
housing.quote: decreasing housing prices and increasing affordable housing opportunities are two of my top priorities

schools.text: Garamendi opposes cuts to public education and backs federal funding to lower class sizes and preserve programs.
schools.quote: Garamendi has consistently spoken out against destructive cuts to all levels of education.

immigration.text: Garamendi supports a fair pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and an end to deportation threats.
immigration.quote: I fervently support policies that would provide these integral members of our community with a fair pathway to citizenship

guns.text: Garamendi backs universal background checks and closing the gun-show loophole.
guns.quote: Universal background checks are overwhelmingly supported by the American public

abortion.text: Garamendi says he supports a woman's right to choose and, as a Pro-Choice Caucus member, works to protect reproductive access.
abortion.quote: As a member of the Pro-Choice Caucus, I am proud to fight to preserve, protect, and advance policies that ensure reproductive autonomy for all Americans.

health.text: Garamendi wants to expand Medicare, including letting it negotiate drug prices and adding dental and vision coverage.
health.quote: Lower prescription drug costs in Medicare through the importation of drugs from countries with rigorous safety standards

energy.text: Garamendi calls the climate crisis serious and champions clean-energy investment.
energy.quote: Congressman Garamendi is a passionate advocate for investments in clean energy, building weatherization, public transit, and biking amenities

voting.text: Voted for the For the People Act, which he described as expanding voting rights.
voting.quote: Rep. Garamendi voted to pass H.R. 1, the “For the People Act,” a sweeping anti-corruption package to clean up Washington, protect and expand voting rights, restore integrity to government and put the needs, and priorities of the American people ahead of special interests.

tax.text: Recile argued against raising taxes on the wealthy, saying it would drive away the businesses that create jobs, and separately called government spending out of control.
tax.quote: The billionaires are the ones that are bringing in industry, and if you start taxing them they can just pick up and move.

wages.text: Spoke at a news conference opposing a proposed $30 minimum wage, warning that it could cause businesses to close or cut jobs.
wages.quote: A sudden jump to $30 an hour minimum wage could force them to close their businesses, cut jobs, raise hours, raise prices or close altogether,

housing.text: Recile faulted local governments for making it hard to build homes in California, favoring easier home development.
housing.quote: have made it very difficult for developers to develop homes, especially in California.

schools.text: Recile calls for expanding school choice, saying education funding should follow the student and backing nationwide tax credits for schooling.
schools.quote: Money should follow the child not the child following the money.

immigration.text: Said Congress should ensure immigration laws are enforced as written and that immigrants need to follow the law.
immigration.quote: From the House's side of it, we just need to make sure that the law is being enforced as it's written,”

energy.text: Recile praised U.S. energy independence and high domestic production, and elsewhere called nuclear the cleanest and safest energy source.
energy.quote: The USA was producing so much energy the USA was selling energy to other countries.
